photos.c: BOTTOM CENTRE: Laurie O'Hara races for the final change-over.

The Brighton in PHOTOS: TOP LEFT: Pat Newell takes the baton from Bill Kerr to set off on Stage 10 with a 2 minutes lead. TOP RIGHT: Laurie O'Hara gives Gerry North the lead we all hoped for---46 secs over Portsmouth after 7 stages. John Davies, behind, takes a time-check. CENTRE LEFT: That long stretch of empty road behind Gerry North lengthens with every stride. CENTRE RIGHT:Bill Kerr clocks fastest time on Stage 9---the longest at 6 miles-52 yards. BOTTOM LEFT: The picture Eddie Lacey has waited 22 'Brightons' for---Belgrave crossing the line 3mins-10secs ahead of Portsmouth. BOTTOM RIGHT:Alan Black hands the presentation baton to the Mayor of Brighton Councillor S.D. Deason J.P. Photos by E.D.L. & R.L.

THE WINNING LONDON-BRIGHTON RELAY TEAM (Southern Event) ON THE SEA-FRONT WITH THE PRESIDENT AND THE "NEWS OF THE WORLD" TROPHY. REAR:(L.toR.) P. Newell, W.Kerr,Geoff.North,R.Linstead,The President, A.Fairclough,B.Sawyer,C. Dabbs. FRONT:(L.toR.)J.Thresher,Gerald North,L.O'Hara,A. Black. (C.W. Walker was not present).

TOP LEFT: Bill Kerr trails Bullivant and Tulloh on Stage 9. TOP RIGHT: John Thresher hands over to a determined Trevor Hart after stage 2. CENTRE: Alan Mead and 'Noddy' Edwards, with some female assistance, cheer on the runners! BOTTOM LEFT: Laurie O'Hara hands over to Gerry North after chopping 17 secs off the Club record for stage 7. BOTTOM RIGHT: Alan Black brings Belgrave home in 4th place.
THE CLUB '3' (Top, l.to r.) John Bicourt 8th; The start; Jack Brown leads Mike Shingles. (Bottom l.to r.) John Moore 7th, Tony Fairclough 3rd, Laurie O'Hara 2nd, Gerry North 1st (Photos:C. Shippen.)
Gerry North and Alan Black lead Geoff North (1), O'Hara (5), Thorpe (18), Fairclough (16) and Dabbs (27) shortly after the start.

Every inch counts, even after 10 miles slogging across country on a murky January afternoon. Tony Fairclough and Laurie O'Hara fight out the right to hold the "Macher Shield" for 1966 in a thrilling finish. Tony (41) was the winner.

BACKPIECE PHOTOS: TOP LEFT: Barefooted Hart in the throes of a 9 miles battle with Dai Davies (TVH) who pipped him by one place. TOP RIGHT: Bicourt leads Ward (Man.DLC), Billings (Sutt.in A) and team-mate O'Hara. John finished one place ahead of Billings and 23 up on Ward. BOTTOM: A desperate North fights to hold off Bob Holt, Peter Welsh (Empire S'chase gold-medallist) and Mike Turner.
BACK PAGE PHOTO by Ron Linstead -- LAURIE O'HARA sets the pace for GERRY NORTH and PETER WHEWELL at the 5 mile mark of the Club '7' early this month.

PHOTO ACTION AT NATIONAL LEAGUE. TOP LEFT: Dick Piotrowski heads for a ducking in the S/chase, but surfaced to go on to finish 3rd. in 9:30.8 TOP RIGHT: In the 'B' S/chase Alan Black sets the pace and also secured 3rd. position. BOTTOM LEFT: Adrian Major runs at the shoulder of Don Faircloth (Croydon) in the 'A' 5000 metres before he too finished 3rd. BOTTOM RIGHT: In the 'B' 5000 metres Laurie O'Hara proved too good for most of the second strings and he is seen here finishing 2nd.

SWARD TEAM RACE WINNERS
Adrian Major,Laurie O'Hara,John Bicourt,Peter Morris
Fairclough, O'Hara and Piotrowski are all set for some fast road times

THE WINNING "JOHNSTONE" TEAM (Photo:David Hart)
BACK ROW(l.to.r.):G.Biscoe(Manager),A.Fairclough(Reserve),R.Piotrowski,L.O'Hara,P.Morris, P.O'Connor.
FRONT ROW(l.to.r.):G.W.Dance,J.Thresher,Gerry North(Captain),Geoff North,T.Hart.
Note:L. Mann is absent--under escort back to the Palace!.
O'HARA and HART, 3rd and 4th scorers at Coulsdon.
Colin Pearson leads narrowly from John Thresher and Jim Rimmer with Guy Monnet, Laurie O'Hara, Mark McNair and John Keily following up in the Club 1500m championship.
Pat O'Connor leads Laurie O'Hara by six inchen (at a guess) in the "Epsom 10"
Front Cover. Laurie O'Hara on the winners rostrum after the 5,000m final at the International Veterans Meeting at Cologne

Opposite.
Laurie O'Hara (left) and Bill Weller, all smiles after one of the tightest finishes ever seen on our 5¾ mile road course. Both were given 28 minutes 18 seconds but Laurie got the verdict.

NATIONAL VET'S '74

Top: Morris (Birchfield) and Salt (Rochdale) lead the field at the start with Southern Champion Brown/133, Goodfellow/169 and Laurie O'Hara/4 close behind. Centre: At the end of lap 1 the first eight are through and Clive Shippen/7 and Pat Newall/5 lead the chasing field. Bottom: The Belgrave team (with intruder George Brown - former London cross country champion) all smiles after their second successive title win. Left to right - Shippen, Brown, O'Hara and Newall.
Medallists in the 1979 Club '10' C.C. Championship. Left to right: Ian Duncan (1st), Laurie O'Hara (2nd) and Jim Rimmer (3rd).
Back Page: Two of Belgrave's long serving stalwarts. Laurie O'Hara hands over to Lionel Mann during the 100 x 1 mile relay.
Good packing in the 3rd Surrey League Race. Simon Holmes leads Bob Richardson and Laurie O'Hara with Junior John Searle having a fine run in close attendance.

Still bunched in the Club 5000m Championship. Ley Coy leads from Laurie O'Hara and Tony Binda followed by; Tony Fairclough,Simon Williamson,Leo Lyons(hidden),Martin Head(94),Bill Downey(95) and Tony Grant(40)

West side story. 1 mile into the 5¾ and the field is bunched waiting for the break. Following Mark Sinclair and John Gladwin are Bob Lettin(71), Leo Coy, Olly Foote, Laurie O'Hara, Mike Nouch,Eric Crutcher(70),Martin Lake,Simon Williamson(68),and Keith Sinclair(22).

Above; The remarkable Laurie O'Hara,who, at the age of 51, still managed to make our Southern 12 stage team following his great run in the Southern Counties Veterans Championships when he won the Over 50's by a record 85 seconds margin.
Laurie O'Hara still has always had a devastating finish. Here he storms home in the Home Countries M60 International, having just taken 17 seconds out of Eric Appleby in the final burst.
Mr. Dependable - Laurie O'Hara.
Left: He just goes on and on ... Laurie O'Hara placed 2nd in the over 50 3000 metres in a record time (for an M60) of 10:09.1

Laurie O'Hara traverses Farthing Downs, Coulsdon, during the final Surrey Cross Country League fixture of the 1969-70 season. Belgrave took the team race and topped the League for the 5th consecutive year.
We will always remember Laurie O'Hara as a winner. The Dysart Dash 10k at Petersham on June 30th 1996 was one of Laurie's very last races and yet again he was the first man home in his category.

Left: Enjoying the occasion.  Pat Mead, Tony Binda, Marianne Black, Gerry North, Alan Black, the late Laurie O'Hara, George Piddington, Charlie Henn, Ted Pallant, Chris Steer, Charlie Manning.

Sadly this was the last time that we saw Laurie O'Hara.  He died the following day while out running.
